verdict.rationale: Community reports describe npm's own native config settings for both named protections: `ignore-scripts=true` blocks lifecycle scripts and `min-release-age=7` enforces a minimum release age. Both can be set in ~/.npmrc, and the first-party docs confirm config can be set by env var or CLI flag. Scripts still run by default, but the story only asks that the protections can be turned on. missing for 10: first-party documentation of ignore-scripts and min-release-age, organization-wide or centrally enforced policy controls, protections beyond these two settings.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can turn on protections against malicious packages, such as blocking lifecycle scripts or enforcing a minimum release age

citations.quote: npm now supports a minimum release age. Put `min-release-age=7` (days) and `ignore-scripts=true` in ~/.npmrc.
The commenter recommends setting ignore-scripts=true in ~/.npmrc
Set any config by prefixing the name in an environment variable with `NPM_CONFIG_`.
